Thanks for this, and sorry it sat for so long.

We are not taking it, but the reason is not the implementation. We already have a colour accessibility setting on the Pro side that is likely to come across to Community, and a separate due date colour scheme next to it would leave us with two settings doing overlapping work.

If the motivation here was readability for colour vision deficiency rather than preference, say so and we will make sure that need is covered when that setting lands.

We are not taking this one.

The endpoint returns every card where the current user is a member or the
author, and checks nothing else. Everywhere else in the API a card is reached
through its board and the controller confirms the board membership first. This
one does not, so somebody who created a card on a board they were later
removed from still gets that card back, with its labels, tasks, attachments
and custom field values.

There is also no limit and no paging, so the response grows with the instance,
and `included` carries memberships whose users are not in it, which a client
cannot resolve.

The want behind it is reasonable. Scoped through board membership the way
`cards/show` does it, paged, and returning what the response references, it is
something we would look at.

Closing this. Thanks for the work.
